headline: TI-New Source guidelines kept unchanged; parked CROP applications revived once (as fresh files); CROP automation plan (auto-issue of 9(4) CRs, drone endorsement category, geo-tagging); Diquat import rejected.

changes.d: After the Drosera appeal order, the RC found no reason to amend the TI-New Source requirements; they are scientifically justified and must be followed.

changes.t: Parked applications revived, one time only
changes.d: About 353 parked Import Permit, Form-I and endorsement applications were revived (public notice 30.03.2026). They become fresh files with a new number and date; no further requests will be accepted.

Plan: CRs of already-registered biopesticide strains issued from the strain data bank; 9(4) TIM/TI CRs issued automatically as mirror images of 9(3); address changes update accounts automatically; a separate drone endorsement category; corrigenda attached to CRs; geo-tagging of premises. Old 'completed' endorsements listed for comments.
Sharda's Diquat 200 g/L FI rejected for unacceptable data, its banned/restricted status abroad and high toxicity.

changes.t: Household use needs a household application
changes.d: Syngenta's label expansions for household pests were rejected; such products must be filed under the household category with full data.

changes.t: Label expansion under FIM vs FI
changes.d: No separate bio-efficacy data; the revised label/leaflet is issued as per the endorsement on the FIM certificate.

changes.t: 9(3B) extensions and the Madras High Court
changes.d: After the Division Bench judgment of 23.03.2026, extensions already granted continue, subject to the writ petitions' outcome.
FCI asked for bio-efficacy and residue reports on alternative insecticides for grain storage.

actions: Revived parked files: check the new file number and date on CROP.
Household uses: file under the household category, not as a label expansion.
